acceptance_criteria: AC-1: confirm current state before changing anything, report via a short RELAY_NOTE. (a) console/registry_targets.py::resolve_registry_targets/_identity_resolved is the M6/M8.4 admission gate for a device_id-targeted config_refresh_cp job -- it returns a bool, never the resolved entity_id, even though it internally reads `relationship.entity_id` (the ACTIVE M8.1 relationship row) to cross-check evidence. Confirm this reading is still accurate. (b) console/runner.py::_build_argv -> utils.collection_executor.workflow_argv passes the raw submitted `targets` (device_ids) straight through as `--cp-config-targets` for the cp-config workflow, which expects `entity_id`s (its own docstring: 'the physical-host entity_id already used throughout the repository'). Confirm no translation step exists anywhere between admission and argv construction. (c) CRITICAL: console/registry_targets.py's own module comment (near _identity_resolved's trust-currency cross-check) documents that the CP config evidence snapshot metadata `_collect_host` writes today carries NO `host_key_fingerprint` field, so `_identity_resolved`'s final check fails closed (returns False) for EVERY real M8.3-produced relationship, including the one just proven live 2026-09-08 (relationship_id e4671bc45e5e49e2bf9257d32b3fa067, project/backlog.json id m8_3_real_environment_validation) -- meaning the M8.4 admission gate cannot currently pass for any real device, this movement's own wiring included, until that gap closes. Confirm this is still true against current code. A prior movement (M8.4) deliberately left this alone under the instruction 'do not modify the M8.3 producer unless a material defect makes M8.4 impossible' -- that condition now appears to hold. If your investigation confirms (c), this movement's scope MUST include adding host_key_fingerprint to the evidence metadata the physical-host collection primitive (_collect_host, shared by the bulk collector and the M8.3 producer) writes, sourced from the same utils.cp_ssh_trust.host_key_fingerprint the M8.3 producer's own trust lookup already computes -- do not invent a second fingerprint source. If your investigation finds (c) is no longer accurate, or finds a narrower fix, report via RELAY_NOTE and adjust scope accordingly rather than assuming this SESSION_START's framing is still exactly right.

AC-2: build the entity_id-substitution wiring: given an admitted device_id-targeted config_refresh_cp job, resolve each device_id to its currently proven collector entity_id (the same ACTIVE M8.1 relationship the admission gate already reads) and substitute the resolved entity_id(s) -- never the raw device_id(s) -- into the argv passed to --cp-config-targets. Preserve every existing M6/M8.4 admission/eligibility/re-check behavior exactly (resolve_registry_targets's refusal codes, the re-check-immediately-before-execution call in console/runner.py, the fail-closed identity law already documented there) -- this movement adds the missing translation step, it does not relax or duplicate the existing gate.

AC-3: end-to-end functional proof. Real-device confirmation needs the Product Owner to run the actual console job against a real device (per AI_START_HERE.md's Real-environment procedure -- you propose the exact bounded command, you do not execute it) -- report this as a request if reached. At minimum, build a realistic fixture-based test proving: a device_id submitted to config_refresh_cp with a proven relationship resolves to the correct entity_id and that entity_id (not the device_id) appears in the constructed argv; an unproven/stale relationship still refuses exactly as before (no regression to the existing IDENTITY_TRANSLATION_REQUIRED path).

AC-4: no change to any other job type's target handling (entity_ids mode, none mode), no change to the M6/M8.4 refusal codes or their conditions/ordering, no change to the M8.3 producer's own write gate (Section 6/§8 AC1/AC10) beyond the narrow fingerprint-field addition from AC-1(c) if confirmed necessary.

AC-5: targeted tests for the new translation step and (if AC-1(c) is confirmed) the fingerprint metadata addition, following tests/test_m6_registry_keyed_job_targets.py's existing style. AC-6: validation and state: targeted tests green; full one-shot regression once (DEV.TEST.1) since this touches the shared collection_executor/console job path; update project/roadmap.json (m7_real_device_targeted_collect_now: planned -> in_progress/done as appropriate; M12's note if this changes its own reachability), project/feature_registry.json if a relevant criterion closes, CURRENT_STATE.md and project/build_history.json in this PR.

entries.subject: AC-1 investigation: (a)/(b) confirmed, (c) is STALE -- already fixed by PR #103
entries.text:
AC-1(a): confirmed, code unchanged -- console/registry_targets.py::_identity_resolved still returns bool, never the resolved entity_id, though it reads relationship.entity_id internally (line ~161-181).
AC-1(b): confirmed, code unchanged -- console/runner.py::_execute passes record.targets (raw device_ids) straight to _build_argv -> utils.collection_executor.workflow_argv, which places them verbatim after --cp-config-targets (collection_executor.py line ~249). No translation step exists anywhere in this path.
AC-1(c): NOT accurate against current code -- the gap this SESSION_START describes was already closed by project/build_history.json's 'm8_evidence_host_key_fingerprint_not_persisted' (PR #103, merged 2026-09-07, merge commit 06e51d36a11ed2ecc8dfc4d7581656aa09c5c95d), BEFORE this SESSION_START (2026-09-08 19:22:48Z) was issued. configuration/checkpoint_config_collector.py::_collect_host's physical-host store.write_text_snapshot(...) call already includes host_key_fingerprint: key_fp in extra_metadata (line ~1596), sourced from the same _connect()/utils.cp_ssh_trust fingerprint _identity_resolved's own trust lookup uses -- exactly the fix AC-1(c) asks for, already shipped. console/registry_targets.py's own comment above the evidence_fingerprint check (lines ~193-207) and tests/test_m8_4_m6_resolver_consumption.py::_fully_resolved's docstring (lines ~141-146) are the only things still describing the closed gap as current fact; both are now stale prose, not a functional defect. tests/test_m8_4_m6_resolver_consumption.py::test_evidence_missing_fingerprint_still_fails_closed already reflects the fix (renamed and re-documented as part of PR #103) and correctly keeps only the defensive fail-closed-on-absent-fingerprint case, not the general-case gap.
Scope adjustment: AC-1(c)'s conditional fingerprint-metadata fix is NOT needed -- dropping it from this movement's scope. Proceeding with AC-2 (entity_id-substitution wiring) only, plus correcting the two stale-comment locations identified above as part of this movement's own housekeeping (no functional change to _collect_host or the M8.3 producer).
